4. In view of the said order, initially, the petitioners have already deposited Rs.1,20,000/- and also deposited Rs.9,00,000/-.
The amount of Rs.30,000/- is also deposited after the same is pointed out to the learned counsel for the petitioners.
Thus, the contents of the settlement terms have already been complied with by the petitioners.

5. In view of the observation of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab and another reported in MANU/SC/0781/2012 wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court observed that where the High Court quashes a criminal proceeding having regard to the fact that the dispute between the offender and the victim have been settled, although the offences are not  (4) 3.wp.607.2016 compoundable, it does so as in its opinion,
continuation of criminal proceedings will be an exercise in futility and justice in the case demands that the dispute between the parties is put to an end and peace is restored, securing the ends of justice being the ultimate guiding factor.

sentences.text:
In this regard a specific reference was made to offences arising out of matrimony, particularly relating to dowry, etc. or a family dispute, where the wrong is basically to victim but the offender and victim have settled all disputes between them amicably, irrespective of the fact that such offences have not been made compoundable.
The High Court may, within the framework of its inherent power, quash the criminal proceeding or criminal complaint or F.I.R if it is satisfied that on the face of such settlement, there is hardly any likelihood of the offender being convicted and by not quashing the criminal proceedings, justice shall be casualty and ends of justice shall be defeated.
6.

Though the offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC is non-compoundable,
considering the dispute is in the nature of matrimonial dispute and the parties already have arrived at a settlement.
There is no hesitation in accepting the prayer to quash the FIR.

At the same time, it is clear that the respondent No.3 i.e. original complainant, is at liberty to withdraw the said amount along with accrued interest on the amount of Rs.1,20,000/-, which was already deposited.
